content:
incident-bot: paging SRE_Oncall: High severity alert: edge POP 'galaxy-eu-central' announcing stale/partial DNS routes + packetloss to select ISPs. Affected prefix: 203.0.113.0/24.
SRE_Oncall: Acked. I’m awake, joining. Can someone drop the last 2 mins of pcap from the POP?
Alice Park: @SRE_Oncall grabbing pcap now from the POP. I see 20-40% packet loss from our egress to CarrierNet and TransitOne during the last 5m.
SRE_Oncall: Good. Initial hypothesis: BGP announcement race after a config push caused partial withdraw and then reannounce with wrong communities -> some upstreams blackholed. Also seeing increased DNS NXDOMAINs from the authoritative for our CDN edge.
Ben Ortiz: I’m spinning up traffic to the fallback pool and will re-route origin pulls to eu-west1. Putting CDN edge into "safe-mode" (no new caching) to reduce churn.
Priya Shah: SupportBot, flag customers in EU region with >2xx drop and >500ms p50.
SupportBot: Noted. Querying metrics... matching customers: 8 accounts show elevated errors, 3 exhibit request timeouts. Creating support tickets.
SRE_Oncall: Steps: 1) coordinate with NetworkVendorOps to validate BGP announcements 2) lower authoritative DNS TTL and re-check delegation 3) steer traffic to backup POPs 4) keep customers notified.
NetworkVendorOps: We see intermittent withdraws from galaxy-eu-central to TransitOne ASN 64501. Looks like our AS path prep got applied intermittently. Upstream confirmed they saw flaps. We're in contact.
Diego Marquez: Can we temporarily withdraw the problematic prefix from the POP and announce a /25 from backup to force reroute?
SRE_Oncall: Yes, prepare a controlled withdraw. Alice, can you stage the withdraw and route announce? I’ll coordinate with upstreams.
Alice Park: Running the withdraw now:
```
# at POP
vtysh -c 'configure terminal' -c 'no router bgp 64496' -c 'ip route 203.0.113.0/24 null0'
# announce backup via eu-west1 fabric
vtysh -c 'configure terminal' -c 'router bgp 64496' -c 'network 203.0.113.128/25'
```
Alice Park: Withdraw completed and /25 announced via eu-west1 fabric. Confirming BGP converged on TransitOne.
NetworkVendorOps: Upstream confirms they now see the /25 from eu-west1 as the best path. Packet loss to those prefixes is dropping to ~1-2%.
SRE_Oncall: Nice. Now DNS: reduce TTL to 60 on authoritative names so resolvers refresh quickly. Priya, can you apply via the DNS console?
Priya Shah: TTL change applied to CDN edge records. Propagation underway. Also lowered healthcheck thresholds to avoid flapping.
Emma Li: Observability: p95 latency in EU is still high (~900ms) but trending down. Error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after the announce.
Product-Eng: Any customer-facing incident message draft? We should tell impacted users we’re rerouting traffic and investigate root cause.
SupportBot: Draft created in #support-drafts. Link: https://redwood.kb/incidents/2123456789/draft (auto).
SRE-ShiftLead: Heads up — I’ll be taking the rotation handoff in 18 minutes. If anything critical happens I’ll join. @SRE_Oncall please prepare a quick summary for the handover.
SRE_Oncall: Summary: galaxy-eu-central experienced BGP announce regress after a config push; partial withdraws caused traffic blackholing to some ISPs and caused DNS anomalies. Mitigations: withdrew prefix at POP and announced /25 via eu-west1 fabric, lowered DNS TTL, put CDN cache-safe-mode, shifted origin pulls. Current status: packetloss reduced, recovery in flight.
Alice Park: Throwing an immediate health test to confirm cache integrity and origin pull success.
SRE_Oncall: Confirmed origin pulls via eu-west1 succeed. Canary traffic shows stable responses.
NetworkVendorOps: We also requested a deeper hardware health check at the POP — fabric control plane reported transient CPU spikes during the config push window. Vendor will follow up with logs.
Diego Marquez: Any customer impact numbers?
Emma Li: Short window (approx 7 minutes) where some ISPs experienced 30-40% packetloss, about 18% elevated application errors for EU traffic overall. Approx 1.2k requests failed across 8 customers. Most recovered after reroute.
Product-Eng: Noting churn for sessions — session-resume is working for most but a small fraction (approx 0.8%) saw incomplete responses; we should surface to product incident page.
SupportBot: Support tickets for impacted customers created: TKT-19821, TKT-19822, TKT-19823. Templates attached.
SRE-ShiftLead: I’m taking handoff now. @SRE_Oncall please paste the mitigation commands and any pending vendor actions.
SRE_Oncall: Mitigation commands in conversation above. Pending vendor actions: vendor to provide POP fabric control-plane logs and confirm whether the config push triggered the CPU spike; TransitOne to confirm they didn’t apply any local policy that would have amplified the withdraw.
NetworkVendorOps: Vendor acknowledged and will send logs to ops@networkvendor within 2h. We also recommended a safe rollout policy for BGP config pushes.
Alice Park: For follow-up: add a preflight check for community prep and simulate a withdraw in staging. Filing follow-up ticket: OPS-4287.
Product-Eng: I’ll coordinate the customer communication plan and CS will send proactive notices to the top affected accounts.
SRE-ShiftLead: Current severity: degraded, customer impact contained. Keeping channel open until confirmed vendor logs and metrics back to baseline for 2h. If anything regresses, escalate immediately.
SRE_Oncall: Leaving a note: reflections — add BGP announcement canary for 30s before wide push; enhance DNS monitoring for authoritative mismatch.
SupportBot: Sending final incident summary to #incident-summaries in 30m.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by SRE_Oncall at 2123460000.
SRE-ShiftLead: Thanks everyone, I’ll track the vendor deliverables and update the postmortem.
Alice Park: grabbed heap of PCAPs and saved to s3://redwood-incidents/2123456789/pcaps/ for postmortem.
Diego Marquez: Adding a note for networking: review our AS path prep automation.
Product-Eng: Closing loop with support after we confirm baseline.
SRE_Oncall: Signing off — leaving channel to oncall lead.
SRE-ShiftLead: Acknowledged, taking over monitoring.
